I see a couple of issues with the inline YouTube player that you get when YouTube is linked from a comment, such as here for example.

I think there should be a setting in the preferences to disable the inline YouTube player.

I think the YouTube thumbnail logo should be a link to go directly to YouTube and watch the video there, even if the link text still points to the inline YouTube player because that's still enabled in the preferences.

When the user clicks through to YouTube (currently via the Open link that only shows up after clicking to show the inline player first; in the future hopefully also more directly, as per the above), YouTube should open in the current window and tab by default, not in a new window/tab, as it currently does.

The inline player has problems, because there is a variety of ways in which YouTube URLs can be formed, and those ways have changed in the past and may change in the future. For the inline player to work correctly, it has to reimplement all that, feature by feature, which it currently does not do. In the above example, the URL is one with a time parameter, the &t=7m20s, which should play the video from 7 minutes, 20 seconds into the clip, every time the link is clicked. The inline player does not do that now. It actually plays the video from the start or from where you last stopped watching that link (a confusing misfeature if the link has a time parameter). Note that &t=7m20s is just one of the ways in which the time parameters can be written; it can also be written all in seconds, or only in minutes, and it can occur in various places of the URL. Then there's also a #-prefixed time parameter, which is a different feature and—on YouTube—works differently, and only points users to the parameter-specified time the first time round, and thereafter also plays from where the user last stopped watching. This is different from the &-prefixed time parameter, which—on YouTube—always plays from the specified time (though that doesn't work correctly inline on voat). It goes without saying that time parameters not working correctly could disrupt discussions because it will lead to viewers not seeing what the poster meant to point them to, in a potentially long video.

If all of this seems complicated, and very complicated to correctly reimplement, the message should be clear: Don't force the inline player on users, because it will likely always be subtly or not-so-subtly flawed. Don't make it the default, make it an experimental feature users can opt into in their preferences, or at least allow users to disable it in their preferences.

As tempting as "web2.0ey" features like an inline YouTube player may be, just because you can, doesn't mean you should. There is merit in the KISS principle. A simple hyperlink like any other would in many ways be much more functional.

If there's any merit at all in voat reinventing the wheel by partially reimplementing YouTube with that inline player, then that merit might be in adding a useful feature YouTube itself currently lacks: The ability to specify a time at which to stop playing. (YouTube currently allows you to specify a start time, but not an end time. There was a site, splicd.com, which used to allow the latter, but that site is offline now.)

I own and moderate two decently-sized subs, /v/seriousdiscussion and /v/customizingvoat. Here are some tips I've observed:

  1. The community itself will be the biggest factor to grow your subverse. Your subverse expands well when the common denominator increases. Posting a lot of quality links will help, but others, who have a different perspective than you but still share your interests, who post links they like will potentially attract users who weren't interested enough to subscribe because of your personality.

    Take /v/seriousdiscussion as an example. I post occassionally to keep the subverse alive, but most of those posts hover around 4-8 points and 60-80 views each on average. @tc_thwarting, with a different perspective on the other hand, made a post that scored 24 points with 211 views. A post I would have never made.

  2. Your participation is the second-biggest factor in both keeping your subverse alive and helping it grow. Posting good links, commenting on others' posts, keeping your subverse junk-free, and targeting the vision of your subverse to your community's growing interests will be the deciding factor between the death and growth of a sub.
  3. Advertising your subverse will help. As Voat grows, it's going to get harder for your subverse to become known. Advertising it when completely relevant will both keep your subverse's public image good (even for those who don't want to subscribe) and will let others know that your subverse exists. It is important to only advertise after you've submitted a few of your best links so it's not a wasteland and it'll tell people what your sub's vision is.

There are so many factors that will make your subverse grow, but it would take a long time to share with you all of my observations. Nevertheless, I hope these tips help you. :-)
